The smoker is of great quality simple to use and Trager's customer service is second to none. I also enjoy the support from Traeger with the warranty recipe updates in my inbox and the community which is also passionate about good BBQ. Like anything you're only as good as your tools and my Pro 22 makes BBQing so simple and enjoyable. Thank you Traeger!

Results.ReviewText: I have never been so impressed with a grill as I am with this Pro Series 34! NOT THIS TIME! I used NO sauce (just the dry rub at the beginning) and left the grill alone at 325 degrees. One and one half hour later my family was eating the moistest most tender and delicious pork we've ever had. I am a huge fan of this grill and can't wait to try other meats on it!!

Results.ReviewText: This grill is unreal. I was back and forth between this and a certain popular large green grill you may have heard of. I chose this due to its versatility simplicity portability and overall fantastic buying process.   First the size. I was between this and a bigger one but was assured this would be plenty big. It looks small in pics but you should go see one at a Traeger dealer. Looks bigger in person. I cooked two large rib racks 40 chicken wings and a skillet full of jalapeno poppers on it at one time with a little room to spare.   It's super easy to start up and maintain a temp. It keeps itself anywhere you choose between 225 and 450 with ease. If you open the cover it'll drop of course but gets back to temp very quickly.   I've made ribs pulled pork steaks burgers chicken breast chicken wings and lots of veggies on it so far (had it not even 2 weeks). They've all been great except the chicken breast. That might have been my fault though.   I didn't realize it until I was comparing models but the saw horse legs really made a difference. It seems so much more sturdy than other grills even from Traeger. It's good because I roll it regularly from my patio to my garage and it's super easy with the wheels and the sturdy legs.   The only negative I have about it is that the meat probes aren't instant read. It takes a minute for them to catch up but if you leave the probes in you won't have any problems. Also a 5 gallon bucket doesn't really fit between the hopper clean out and the legs so you could spill some pellets if your'e not careful. By no means a deal breaker but something to keep in mind when using it.   Everything from buying the grill setting up the grill to using the grill has been fantastic. The sales experience was amazing before during and after the sale. There's a million recipes online and all sorts of sites/communities dedicated to these. I highly recommend you look into this. I'm Traeger's newest biggest fan.

Took 15 minutes to unpack and within the hour we were cooking chickens and watching the magic happen. Results.ReviewText: The Pork Butt is ready. The Traeger Smoker is ready set at 225 deg. I placed the 11 pound pork butt all dressed up and rubbed up in a aluminum pan took both built in digital probes and inserted one on each side of the butt (this is not necessary just wanted to see how consistent this smoker really is) covered the butt with aluminum foil placed it on the smoker shut the lid and walked away. 8 hours later both probes were reading 212 deg. internal temp of the butt. Based on the normal rule of thumb 1-1/2 hours per pound cooking/smoking time I calculated 16.5 hours to cook this Butt. After 8 hours 'BAM' were making Food Coma History. Traeger Grill/Smokers are AMAZING. If you value your time get one of these Grill/Smokers you'll have time to spent with family and friends you never new existed before because you were to busy trying to keep your other grill/smoker consistent.
Results.Title: The Life of a 11 Pound Pork Butt

Results.ReviewText: I am a long time BBQ lover a backyard (my own) pit boss and a compitition BBQ judge. I always thought using a pellet grill was let's say taking the easy way our maybe even cheating. I had an off set stitch burner for many years and I could produce some pretty good Q on it if I do say so myself. I started spending a little time with my buddy Chad at his BBQ supply store. After seeing and tasting what he was pulling off of his traegers I began to soften my position on the pellet grilles.  Well last November I did it. I became a pellet head. I purchased a Pro 22. I gave my stick burner to my nephew and have not regretted it for a second. There is most definitely a learning curve and I am learning. I have done spatchcock Cornish hens wings St. Louis ribs Boston butt and some killer bacon wrapped pork tenderloins. Everything has turned out as good or mostly better than anything I produced on the stick burner. I could never see myself going back to the all day long fire fighting that my old grill required. I love my new Traeger and look forward to pulling something out of the freezer every weekend. Happy q-en to ya David

Results.ReviewText: Ok people here's the deal. All my life I've been a hard-core stick smoker. Last year I purchased the Traeger Renegade Elite. Cool beans AWESOME GRILL cooked everything I could think of cooking on this grill just put it on and walk away until it's done. Until the day it happened. The day my sweet girlfriend said 'Hey can you cook beef jerky on that grill' I smoked 2lbs of sirloin tip cut into jerky strips and marinated in my own recipe (I now have four different marinates) she ate the end product and instantly went into a FOOD COMA. I took some to work and was asked by all co-workers that tried it until there was no more so how much do you sell this jerky for? This is the best jerky they've ever tasted. I was taken back by the question and said I'll let ya'll know tomorrow. In one week I sold 10 pounds of cured beef jerky. I told my son who works for a aircraft plant about the homemade beef jerky I was making. He now receives 30 pounds of Wild Bill's cured Beef Jerky a week from me every week to keep up with supply and demand. I sold my used Traeger grill to a friend and the cost difference for upgrading from the Renegade to the Pro Series 34 was paid for in 3 weeks from jerky sales. I am able to smoke 9 pounds of jerky meat at a time on this grill using the smoke rack for a total of 1244 sq in of cooking space. This is a awesome grill to own and a money maker if you work it right. Moral of this TRUE story is ' Go BIG or GO HOME '

Results.ReviewText: I have always wanted a Traeger Pellet Grill but needed the bravery to spend the money. After using twice over the Labor Day Holiday the wait and money was worth it. Purchased at Karls Hardware their knowledge is an added feature to selling me!-2- minor issues that kept me from rating the Traeger FIVE Stars across the board. #1 The unit was well packaged with one exception under the main unit- an ultra heavy duty cardboard piece protects that portion....under the Pellet Box- no additional packaging was present. This was a result of one corner and side being bent. Although minor you would hope with a heavy unit this would be considered. #2 Probably being a little too critical- using an 2 gallon bucket to empty the Pellet Box the clean-out is located too close to the leg and pellets fly out hitting the edge of the bucket.Season the Grill with Oak....which was amazing.First use was with Tri-Tips and Elk Roast using pecan pellets. Our guests wanted a milder smoke- this was why I selected pecan. The dual meat probes were a huge plus with smoking perfection. This was a hit!Second use was Baby Back Ribs using pecan pellets. My family absolutely loved them.After years of experimenting with charcoal and propane wood chip smokers the ease consistency and finished product with a Traeger- is your Ultimate Experience....no more experimenting! Cant wait to Traeger again with burgers and a pizza!

Results.ReviewText: Hello.  I had a friend who was a butcher at a very big butcher shop in Portland Oregon.  After tasting his food many times he shared with me what it was he was cooking his BBQ meats on - a Traeger!  Well he just raved about this grill and he even had a local show on TV  to show how he used his grill to make the most fabulous dinners.We decided then to purchase one of our own.  I purchased the 34 inch grill......back then I think it was the only grill that Traeger offered - this was in the late 90s..  Anyway we bought and loved it.  We would have large BBQ parties throughout the years.  We were known for our 4th of July parties.  We would have many families over.... I would smoke over 6 turkeys and about 6 pork butts for pulled pork for our 4th of July party.  The Traeger sure helped out our cooking time and the taste was far superior to that of regular wood smoking.As a hint since our parties were so huge we would smoke our meats about two weeks before the party. Before the party.   After the meat was cooked to perfection we would vacuum seal them in one of those units that take out all the air and vacumn seal them - we would slice the meat and put them in to the bags we created with the vacuum sealer.  In the turkey bags we would put turkey broth some orange juice and seasonings and seal it up.  In the pulled pork one we would shread the pork and add some BBQ sauce along with some beef broth and seal those.  We would then put them in our deep freeze and on the day of the party we would take them out and put them in big large pots of boiling water - the bags could be put directly in it without them breaking open.  We would then boil the bags till the meat was hot and then take them to chafing pots and cut them open.  Sure cut a lot of time and it made it easy for us to be with our company instead of cooking in front of them!Our Traeger weathered quite a few huge parties and did us well.  We probably used our grill at least 3 to 4 times a week yearround.  After `12 years my wife decided we needed new - she loved the new 34 pro grill with the bronze finish and so we finally broke down and bought a new one.  I love the additional features it now has with the two probes (which make it a lot easier to judge cooking times) and the variety of settings compared to our old unit old faithful.We are a Traeger family and will always be.  We love the unit and I have always had a good experience with any phone calls that I have made.  I even broke down and bought a litlle tex for our motorhome so we are never without our Traeger.
Results.Title: Owned a Traeger for over 12 years
